name: PUC Rio
overview:
PUCs are the largest private, not-for-profit universities in the country. They are at the forefront of research in many areas (both technological and human sciences). They build bold partnerships with companies, notably Petrobras in Rio. The PUC Rio business incubator is of the highest quality. Cooperation with France is carried out with reputable establishments and they have been pioneers in the implementation of double degrees, the use of Brafitec, etc. The PUC Rio, created in 1941, has the Genoa business incubator on its campus. Many previously incubated companies already operate in their own offices and are independent of the university.

The university now receives 20,000 students from very different ethnic and social backgrounds.

PUC RIO is located in Gavea, a charming area next to the forest and the beaches of the southern area of Rio de Janeiro. The campus is located in a tropical forest, surrounded by lush vegetation.
administrative:
1. Application Dossier

You will work directly with the partner university regarding your application. All required documents will have to be uploaded on their platform or sent by email before the deadline (see the Americas Teams channel for each application deadline). If you have not received anything yet, it means your nomination has not been sent yet, please be patient.


In the past the partner has asked for the following:

  • Confirmation of online registration on the Brazilian University website
  • Your transcripts in English
  • A letter of nomination (to be provided by the IAFF department)
  • A cover letter in English
  • Copy of passport (valid at least six months from entry into Brazil with at least two blank pages)
  • A 3 x 4 cm identity photo
  • Medical insurance in English
  • Document proving vaccine against yellow fever
  • A wire transfer sent to Faculdades Católicas referring to the participation on the Pre-Term Portuguese as a Second Language Intensive course and the Registration fee (if taking the course). Please refer to http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccci/incoming/fees_tuition.html to get more information about the tuition, fees and wire transfer details.
  • Attention: For the regular term course, an administrative cost will be charged. Also, in case you have already done the payment, do not forget to send the university a copy of the payment receipt. Otherwise, you will be charged upon arrival.


To be given to EPITECH bachelor campus administration to reenroll for the Tech4 (in April/May):

  • The addendum to the contract
  • EPITECH re-registration dossier


This information is subject to change by the partner university. They will provide you with the most current information upon your acceptance.


2. Visa

In France: student visa

Once your Application dossier has been accepted by PUC Rio, the last step is to obtain your student visa. Obtaining a visa is not automatic, each embassy being sovereign. If you are not a European citizen, please note that the procedure can take up to 3 months. Please note that a tourist visa CANNOT be changed into a student visa once in the country.


Make sure to follow the steps indicated on the Brazilian Embassy here.


You will need to provide proof of financial capacity to apply for a student visa for Brazil: for scholarship students, you'll need to hand out a certificate of scholarship where the monthly amount received must be indicated and give the duration of the scholarship. For non scholarship students, you need to give proof of your ability to support youself for the entire duration of the stay (pay slip, income tax sheet from parents).


Arrival in Brazil: residence permit

When you arrive in Brazil, you will have to go to the Federal Police to register and obtain a Residence Permit (Registro Nacional de Estrangeiro - RNE)


To do this, you must make an appointment in advance and present yourself in person with the requested documents.


You will also have to pay two taxes, the “Registro de Estrangeiros” — R$ 64.58 (around 24€) and the “Carteira de Estrangeiro de Primeira Via” — R$ 124.23 (around 45€)

You need to have a Tax Identification Number (Cadastro de Pessoas Fisicas - CPF) to be able to open a bank account or buy a phone in Brazil.


You can request it at an agency of the Banco do Brasil, Caixa Econômica Federal, or at Correios (Brazilian postal service).


3. Insurance and Health

Rio de Janeiro and Brazil have a number of internationally respect private hospitals, clinics and doctors, but treatment may be expensive.

It is imperative that you take out insurance that will cover you for your medical and hospital expenses, repatriation and accompanied by civil liability. International insurance must cover the entire period of your studies in the country. Insurance costs are the responsibility of each student.


To take out international insurance, the market is quite open. Please click here for more information.


For more information, you can consult the country's health file at: https://www.pasteur.fr/fr/centre-medical/preparer-son-voyage/bresil


Note: It is advisable to register on the French register established outside France and to report to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs via the Ariane platform: https://pastel.diplomatie.gouv.fr/fildariane/dyn/public/login.html.


4.Prepare your arrival

To find out more about advice to travelers issued by the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs on the host country, click here.

Access PUC Rio's pre-departure manual here.

Check out PUC Rio's FAQ for incoming students here.

Discover life in Rio de Janeiro here.


5.Campus life

The campus offers students many facilities: 5 libraries, a computer center, free internet access, campus restaurants, cafeterias and bookstores, a cultural center, etc.
accomodation:
On-campus accommodation

PUC Rio does not have university accommodation.


Off-campus accommodation

  • Host families (more information here)

PUC Rio University does not have university accommodation, but the accommodation service (housing-ccci@puc-rio.br) is responsible for placing students with host families. We strongly recommend that you choose this option which offers more guarantees than other types of accommodation.


Home-stays are located in the south zone of the city, the same as the university, within 30- 40 minutes distance from campus by city bus. However, many students opt to ride to university by bike.


The host families are recommended by CCCI and represent a wide range of incomes and situations. Each house has their specific rules in terms of hygiene, safety, cooking and bringing friends over etc.


Each student will sign a contract, pay the rent upfront during his/her stay, and abide by the house rules. The rent includes a private room with a bed, a fan, a weekly change of sheets and towels, access to light and gas and a Brazilian breakfast. Access to kitchen and laundry facilities is also included. Telephone use is to be arranged between the student and the family. Not all homes have internet available. Please be aware that some houses have only shared rooms (2 beds). In this case the rental per student will be lower than the private room.


Starting from the 2025-2 semester, the housing fee will be R$2.500,00 per month (400€), and if a meal option is available (lunch or dinner), the cost will be R$2.875,00 per month (455€).


Please note : due to very high demand, places with host families are limited and you must contact the university as soon as possible to apply, you must return the "accommodation form" to PUC Rio as soon as possible and apply online.


  • Student residences (more information here and here)

Some private companies provide housing for university students. Their infrastructure includes fully furnished rooms, communal areas, and study spaces.

Uliving and Co.Vivere are some of PUC Rio's partners.


  • Private accommodation

International students may prefer to rent an apartment near campus. You can check PUC-Rio Facebook groups. Prices are usually around US$1200- $1500 for a one-bedroom apartment in the neighborhoods near PUC-Rio, like Ipanema and Copacabana. The same type of apartment in Gávea, the neighborhood in which the university is located, costs around US$1.000. The student should be prepared to give a down payment in order to guarantee the apartment.

Private apartments are not usually recommended by CCCI. PUC-Rio is not responsible if the student decides to live in risky places (i.e.; slums) instead of living in an accommodation selected by the CCCI.


Important notes:

  • Please be careful when renting apartments found via the internet. We recommend working with apartment locators specialized in renting and selling real state;
  • Be sure that people with whom you will be sharing an apartment are trustful;
  • In Brazil, the lease contracts are usually performed at 3 years or 3 months. There are many fees, deposits and taxes to pay for formal rental contracts;
  • Request a receipt for each payment;
  • Inform your new address to PUC -Rio immediately after you move in.
courses:
Credits

  • You will have to take 5 classes per semester.
  • To validate your 4th year abroad, you must validate the equivalent of 60 ECTS, i.e., the equivalent of 40 local credits.
  • A Portuguese course is compulsory. You will take a test on your arrival to find out your level and you will be registered for the corresponding course.


Academic calendar (2026)

Cultural and academic orientation and placement test: 6 August

Semester 2: 11 August-14 December

Cultural and academic orientation and placement test: 26 Feb

Semester 1: 2 March-11 July



Department and courses

Classes are taught in Portuguese.

  • Bachelor Ciência da Computação: http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccg/ciencia_computacao.html
  • Bachelor Sistemas de Informação: http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccg/sistemas_informacao.html
  • Bachelor Engenharia da Computação: http://www.puc-rio.br/ensinopesq/ccg/eng_computacao.html


Optional Courses Taught in English

  • MEC 2015: SYSTEM IDENTIFICATION (3 credits)/ Mechanical Engineering

Introduction to system identification and state estimation: classes of models, applications, linear and nonlinear methods. Practical system identification: design of excitation signals, residual-based validation: metrics and correlation methods, structure selection. Linear system identification: batch and recursive least squares. State estimation: Kalman filter, receding-horizon approaches. Nonlinear system identification: benchmark problems, classical and machine learning based approaches.


  • ELE2602: Information Theory and Error Control Coding (3 credits) / Electronic Engineering

The objective of the course is to introduce the fundamentals of information theory and error control coding. The focus is on the concepts and algorithms required in several areas of communications engineering.


  • ADM 9983: Valuation and Real Options (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The objective is to introduce and provide the student with the concepts and tools required to price assets, value projects and firms and make capital budgeting decisions under uncertainty. We will discuss how risk analysis and simulation models can be of help in the investment decision, and introduce the concept of real option valuation.


  • ADM 9986: ONLINE AND MOBILE MARKETING (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The objective of this course is to introduce students to the concepts and practices involved in a myriad of different Internet Marketing techniques. The goal is to put students in contact with theory and real world Internet applications. Students will explore the key building blocks of the Web and the many ways it can be used as an effective Marketing tool or media. Upon completing this course, students should have a fairly comprehensive knowledge of Internet Marketing and related techniques, with a deep appreciation of their applications and limitations.


  • ADM 9981 MARKETING STRATEGIES THROUGH CONSUMER BEHAVIOR (4 credits) / Admin/Business

Marketing strategies decisions from a consumer behavior approach. Basic determinants of consumer behavior. The roles of marketing as influence on consumer buying and decision making. Impact of consumer behavior on marketing.


  • ADM 998: International Negotiation (4 credits) / Admin/Business

This course is designed to improve your understanding of and skills in international negotiations. After an introduction to the fundamental principles of bargaining and negotiation (including the definition of negotiation, what is negotiable, the golden rule of negotiation, and the role of communication media in negotiations), the course will focus on the essential elements of international negotiations.


  • ADM 9976: INTRODUCTION TO STRATEGY IN A GLOBALIZED WORLD: Global Strategic Management (GSM) (4 credits) / Admin/Business

Basic concepts and tools for strategic management from a global perspective. Assessing and ensuring strategic fit considering global opportunities and challenges. Shift in paradigm of multinational strategies from national differentiation to globalization. International alliances: focus on joint ventures.


  • ADM 2778: International Marketing (3 credits) / Admin/Business

Concepts and practices related to international marketing. Potential markets and identification of opportunities. Analysis of the external environments: economics, legal, cultural and social. International market entry strategies. International marketing strategies: product, services, price, distribution and promotion.


  • ADM 2675: Intermediate Corporate Finance and Governance (3 credits)/ Admin/Business

Corporate capital structure, leverage and debt maturity. Investment policy. Dividend policy. Financial restrictions. Corporate governance and agency theory, private benefits of control, corporate governance mechanisms (ownership structure, board of directors, compensation, takeover market). Investor protection: shareholder protection and creditors rights, and national institutions.


  • ADM 2466: Strategy in changing environment (3 credits) / Admin/Business

This course addresses firm’s strategic responses to the changing environment. As social, environmental, economic and technological changes impacts business as usual, firms must develop capabilities to respond, adapt and compete successfully. The course will bring integrated analyses of dynamic capabilities, managerial capabilities and adaptation literature applied to contexts of environmental uncertainty and turbulence. Classes will include readings, case studies and discussions to provide deeper understanding of the theoretical frameworks and the applied situations.


  • EMP9505: ENTREPRENEURIAL MINDSET (4 credits) / Admin/Business

The course addresses a selected collection of themes that are crucial for the creation and development of a startup, among which one can find group behavior and performance, leadership, motivation and interpersonal influence, storytelling, gamification and design thinking. Through a series of interactive classes, lectures and exercises students develop competencies in organizational design, human resources management, leadership and organizational behavior in the context of an internal or external new venture.


  • HIS 9827: Brazilian History: an introduction (4 credits)/ CONTEXTE LOCAL

This course introduces students to Brazilian History, focusing especially on the social, economic and political changes which took place after the consolidation of Brazilian Republic. Our goal is providing an overview to a variety of topics to understand the historical roots of Brazil today.


  • ELE2765: Adaptive and Array Signal Processing (3 credits) / Electronic Engineering

The objective of the course is to introduce the fundamentals of adaptive and array signal processing using linear algebra, optimisation and intuition. The main focus is on filtering and estimation techniques and beamforming and direction finding methods and their application in several areas of electrical engineering (communications, control, time-series analysis, sensing, defence systems, etc).


  • ELE2707: Stochastic Processes (3 credits) / Math

This course introduces the fundamentals of probability theory, random variables and stochastic processes, and presents the main tools used in the area along with examples often found in electrical engineering and related areas.


Important Notes

  • Presence in class is compulsory, under penalty of loss of visa and repatriation to France at the student's expense (impact on credits).
  • The courses are most likely more academic than at EPITECH.
  • The course list is given for information only. It can change from year to year.
  • If a course is not available when you arrive on site, EPITECH cannot be held responsible for it.
  • Any Tech 4 abroad involves an EIP! Take advantage of the free slots you will have to advance it.
cost:
Financial Overview (4th Year EPITECH)

  • You must pay the tuition fees for the 4th year of EPITECH, as well as the re-registration fees and related fees.
  • EPITECH covers the application fees and part of the tuition fees. Epitech will pay the tuition fees at PUC Rio to the extent of the credits required according to the program followed. Any additional module you wish to take will be at your expense.
  • The tuition supplement payable by you is indicated at the top of this page (if applicable).
  • Other costs at your expense include: travel, accommodation on site, insurance, and everyday expenses (books, food, transport, etc.).


Other expenses

  • Roundtrip flights: about 1000€ depending on the airline & travel dates
  • Insurance: 300-600€ depending on the company and the coverage
  • Visa: about 100€
  • Fees relating to services for international students at PUC Rio: R$ 892.5
  • (To be paid during online registration. This includes: airport pick-up, assistance at the Federal Police (Immigration) registration, welcome lunch, tourist/cultural activities, city tour of Rio de Janeiro, welcome cocktail, field trip, medical assistance on campus, the university ID card, 24/7 psychological assistance, 24/7 emergency cell phone, and a farewell cocktail with live Brazilian music.)
  • Administrative costs: approximately 180€ per semester or 271€ per year


Estimated Monthly Budget

The local currency is the Brazilian Real. 1 € = 6.27 BRL (rate as of October 2025).

Please check the Numbeo website to compare the cost of living between your city of origin and your city of exchange. Please note that everyone's budget will be different according to one's lifestyle.

  • Housing: 500€
  • Food: 90€
  • Transport: 45€
  • Internet; 30€
  • Leisure: 100€


These prices are indicative and may vary.


Additional Information (specifics, advice, useful links, etc.)

  • Withdrawing money: visa electron or cirrus systems are available everywhere. You can withdraw money from almost every bank machine in Rio.
  • Tipping: hotels generally include in the bill any service charges. Tips are discretionary in restaurants but in Brazil the norm is to give a tip. Tips are not expected by taxi drivers although most passengers will round the fare up if they are satisfied with the service.
  • Transport: There are many taxi companies at the airport. If you take a special taxi, you will be charged a fixed fare according to area. Uber is very popular in Rio. For buses, there are numerous urabn bus lines in Rio to reach the campus. The bus ticket is around R$ 4,30 for any path. Bicycles are a good and healthy option of transportation. Students can either buy a bike or use the app "Bike Rio." At night, it is advisable to take a taxi if you go out.
